entries.description: God creates the heavens, the earth, living creatures, and humanity, and rests on the seventh day.
Adam and Eve disobey God in Eden, bringing sin, shame, and expulsion from the garden.
Cain kills his brother Abel after God regards their offerings differently.
God judges widespread human wickedness with a flood while preserving Noah, his family, and animals in the ark.
People build a city and tower to make a name for themselves; God confuses their language and scatters them.
God calls Abram to leave his homeland and promises to bless him and make him a great nation.
God destroys Sodom and Gomorrah while rescuing Lot and his daughters.
God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac, then provides a ram in Isaac’s place.
Jacob dreams of a stairway between earth and heaven and receives God’s covenant promises.
Jacob wrestles through the night, receives a blessing, and is given the name Israel.
Joseph’s brothers sell him to traders, who take him to Egypt.
Joseph explains Pharaoh’s dreams as seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine.
God speaks to Moses from a burning bush and commissions him to lead Israel out of Egypt.
God sends a series of plagues upon Egypt as Pharaoh refuses to release the Israelites.
God instructs Israelite households to mark their doorposts with lamb’s blood, eat the Passover meal, and commemorate his deliverance from Egypt.
God opens a path through the sea for Israel and defeats the pursuing Egyptian army.
God provides manna for the Israelites to eat during their wilderness journey.
God provides water for Israel when Moses strikes a rock at Horeb.
While Moses is on the mountain, the Israelites make and worship a golden calf.
Israel sends twelve men to survey the promised land.
After Israel complains, the LORD sends fiery serpents. Moses raises a serpent of brass, and those who look at it live.
God enables Balaam's donkey to speak after it sees an angel blocking the way.
The Jordan River stops flowing as Israel crosses into the promised land.
Israel marches around Jericho as instructed, and the city walls fall.
Deborah and Barak lead Israel against the army of Sisera.
God delivers Israel from Midian through Gideon and a force reduced to three hundred men.
Delilah discovers the secret connected to Samson’s strength and hands him over to the Philistines.
Ruth meets Boaz while gathering grain, and Boaz later acts as a family redeemer.
Hannah prays for a child and later gives birth to Samuel.
God calls Samuel while he is serving at the sanctuary.
David defeats the Philistine champion Goliath with a sling and stone.
David refuses to kill Saul when he has the opportunity in a cave.
aliases: David Spares Saul in the Cave

entries.description: David takes Bathsheba and arranges the death of her husband Uriah.
aliases: David and Bathsheba on the roof

entries.description: David’s son Absalom rebels against him, leading to conflict and Absalom’s death.
aliases: Absalom's hair caught in a tree

entries.description: Solomon asks God for wisdom to govern the people rather than wealth or long life.
Solomon resolves a dispute between two women claiming the same child.
Solomon dedicates the completed temple, praying before the assembled people of Israel.
Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal, and God answers his prayer with fire.
aliases: Elijah and the Prophets of Baal

entries.description: Elijah is taken up into heaven in a whirlwind as Elisha watches.
Naaman follows Elisha's instruction and is healed of leprosy.
Assyria captures Samaria and exiles many inhabitants of the northern kingdom of Israel.
Babylon captures Jerusalem, destroys the temple, and takes people into exile.
Cyrus permits exiles to return and rebuild the temple.
Nehemiah organizes the rebuilding of Jerusalem’s walls despite opposition.
Esther risks approaching the king to help protect the Jewish people from a planned massacre.
Job loses possessions, children, and health, beginning a prolonged test of his faith.
Three Jewish men are thrown into a blazing furnace for refusing to worship an image and are preserved.
A mysterious message appears at Belshazzar's feast and Daniel interprets it.
Daniel is thrown into a den of lions for praying to God and is delivered unharmed.
Jonah flees from God’s command, is swallowed by a great fish, and prays for deliverance.
Ezekiel sees dry bones restored to life in a vision of Israel's restoration.
The angel Gabriel tells Mary that she will bear Jesus, whose kingdom will have no end.
aliases: Mary told she will have a baby

entries.description: Jesus is born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger; shepherds receive news of his birth.
Wise men from the east follow a star and visit the child Jesus, bringing gifts.
Joseph takes Mary and Jesus to Egypt to escape Herod’s threat and later returns.
aliases: Joseph and Mary flee to Egypt

entries.term: Jesus in the Temple as a Boy
entries.description: At age twelve, Jesus is found among the teachers in the Jerusalem temple.
aliases: The Boy Jesus in the Temple

entries.description: John baptizes Jesus in the Jordan; the Spirit descends and a voice speaks from heaven.
Jesus resists the devil’s temptations in the wilderness by answering with Scripture.
Jesus calls fishermen to follow him.
Jesus teaches about life in God’s kingdom, including righteousness, prayer, and relationships.
Jesus pronounces blessings on people marked by humility, mercy, purity, and faithfulness amid suffering.
Jesus calls his disciples the salt of the earth and light of the world.
Jesus gives his disciples a model prayer honoring God and asking for daily needs, forgiveness, and deliverance.
Jesus teaches his followers to seek lasting heavenly treasure rather than serving wealth.
Jesus teaches his followers not to be consumed by anxiety about food, drink, or clothing.
Jesus encourages persistent prayer through the commands to ask, seek, and knock.
aliases: ask and it shall be given

entries.description: Jesus teaches people to treat others as they would want to be treated.
Jesus contrasts the narrow way to life with the broad way to destruction.
Jesus compares hearing and doing his words to building on rock rather than sand.
Jesus identifies love for God and love for one’s neighbor as the greatest commandments.
Jesus commands his disciples to love one another as he has loved them.
aliases: The Great Commandment to Love One Another

entries.description: Jesus describes himself as the bread of life and teaches about coming to him in faith.
Jesus describes himself as the good shepherd who knows and lays down his life for his sheep.

entries.term: I Am the Resurrection and the Life
entries.description: Jesus tells Martha that he is the resurrection and the life before raising Lazarus.
Jesus tells his disciples that he is the way, the truth, and the life.
aliases: The Way the Truth and the Life

entries.description: Jesus teaches that his disciples bear fruit by abiding in him.
Jesus appears in glory with Moses and Elijah before Peter, James, and John.
Jesus enters Jerusalem riding a donkey as crowds welcome him.
Jesus drives merchants and money changers from the temple. John also records Jesus speaking of the temple of his body.
Jesus teaches about coming troubles, watchfulness, judgment, and his return.
aliases: signs of the end of the age

entries.description: Jesus shares a final meal with his disciples before his arrest and speaks of the new covenant.
aliases: do this in remembrance of me

entries.description: Jesus models humble service by washing his disciples' feet.
Jesus prays in anguish in Gethsemane and submits to the Father's will.
Jesus is seized after Judas identifies him to an armed crowd.
Peter denies knowing Jesus three times before the rooster crows.
Jesus is questioned by the Roman governor before his crucifixion.
Jesus is crucified at Golgotha, where he dies after suffering on the cross.
Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus prepare Jesus' body and place it in a tomb.
The women find Jesus' tomb empty and hear that he has risen.
The risen Jesus explains the Scriptures to two travelers who later recognize him.
Thomas encounters the risen Jesus and believes.
The risen Jesus asks Peter about his love and commissions him to care for his sheep.
The risen Jesus sends his followers to make disciples of all nations.
aliases: go and make disciples of all nations

entries.description: Jesus ascends from his disciples’ sight, and two men in white tell them he will return.
Jesus compares responses to God's word to seed falling on different soils.
Jesus compares the kingdom to a field where wheat and weeds grow until harvest.
aliases: Parable of the Wheat and Tares

entries.description: Jesus likens the kingdom to a tiny seed that grows into a large plant.
Jesus compares the kingdom to yeast that works through a batch of dough.
Jesus compares heaven's kingdom to treasure hidden in a field.
A merchant sells all to obtain a pearl of exceptional value.
aliases: Parable of the Pearl of Great Price

entries.description: Jesus compares the final separation of the righteous and wicked to sorting a catch of fish.
A shepherd searches for one lost sheep and rejoices when it is found.
A woman searches for a lost coin and celebrates when she finds it.
A father welcomes home his younger son after the son wastes his inheritance.
Jesus tells of a Samaritan who shows mercy to a wounded stranger.
A wealthy man stores up possessions but dies before he can enjoy them.
A gardener asks for more time to tend an unfruitful fig tree.
aliases: Parable of the Barren Fig Tree

entries.description: Invited guests make excuses and others are welcomed to a great supper.
Jesus tells of a manager's actions and teaches about faithfulness with wealth.
Jesus tells of a rich man and a poor man whose circumstances reverse after death.
aliases: Parable of the Rich Man and Lazarus

entries.description: A widow repeatedly appeals to a judge in a teaching about persistent prayer.
Jesus contrasts a Pharisee who trusts in his own righteousness with a tax collector who humbly asks God for mercy.
aliases: Parable of the Pharisee and Tax Collector

entries.description: A forgiven servant refuses to forgive a fellow servant's much smaller debt.
Laborers hired at different times receive the same agreed payment.
aliases: Parable of the Workers in the Vineyard

entries.description: Two sons respond differently to their father's request.
Tenant farmers reject and kill the landowner's messengers and son.
A king invites guests to his son's wedding feast and confronts an improperly dressed guest.
Ten virgins wait for the bridegroom; five bring extra oil and are ready when he arrives, while five are not.
Servants are entrusted with money and later give account of how they used it.
Jesus describes the Son of Man judging the nations and separating people as a shepherd separates sheep from goats.
aliases: Parable of the Sheep and Goats

entries.description: Jesus compares God's kingdom to seed growing toward harvest without the farmer knowing how.
aliases: Parable of the Seed Growing Secretly

entries.description: A man asks a friend for bread at midnight; Jesus uses the example to encourage persistent asking in prayer.
aliases: Parable of the Friend at Midnight

entries.description: Jesus changes water into wine at a wedding in Cana.
Jesus heals an official's son from a distance after the official believes his word.
Jesus touches and cleanses a man suffering from leprosy.
aliases: Jesus Heals a Man with Leprosy

entries.description: Jesus forgives and heals a paralyzed man lowered through a roof.
Jesus heals a centurion's servant after the centurion expresses faith in his authority.
Jesus rebukes the wind and sea, bringing calm during a storm.
Jesus frees a man living among tombs from many unclean spirits in the region of the Gadarenes/Gerasenes.

entries.term: Woman with the Issue of Blood
entries.description: A woman suffering prolonged bleeding touches Jesus' garment and is healed.
Jesus raises Jairus' daughter after telling her family not to fear.
Jesus feeds a large crowd using five loaves and two fish.
Jesus walks across the sea toward his disciples' boat.
Jesus feeds a crowd of about four thousand with seven loaves and a few fish.
Jesus gives sight to a man blind from birth, prompting debate about his identity.
Jesus gives sight to Bartimaeus near Jericho.
Jesus heals ten people with leprosy, but only one returns to thank him.
aliases: Jesus Heals Ten Men with Leprosy

entries.description: Jesus calls Lazarus out of his tomb four days after his death.
Jesus directs fishermen to a remarkable catch after an unsuccessful night.
Jesus heals a man who had been disabled for many years.
aliases: Jesus Heals at the Pool of Bethesda
Jesus heals the man at the pool
take up your mat and walk

entries.description: Jesus heals a woman who had been bent over for eighteen years.

entries.term: Healing the Man with a Withered Hand
entries.description: Jesus heals a man's hand on the Sabbath.
aliases: Jesus Heals a Man with a Withered Hand

entries.term: Healing the Deaf and Mute Man
entries.description: Jesus restores hearing and speech to a man brought to him.
aliases: Jesus Heals a Man with a Speech Impediment

entries.description: Jesus heals the ear of the high priest’s servant after one of his followers cuts it off during his arrest.
Jesus instructs Peter to find a coin in a fish's mouth to pay the temple tax.
aliases: Peter finds a coin in a fish

entries.description: Jesus speaks judgment over a fruitless fig tree, which later withers.
Jesus restores a widow's only son to life.
aliases: Jesus Raises the Widow's Son at Nain

entries.description: An angel frees Peter from prison while believers pray for him.
Peter and John encounter and heal a man unable to walk.
aliases: The Healing at the Beautiful Gate
silver and gold have I none

entries.description: Peter prays and Tabitha is restored to life.
Paul restores Eutychus after the young man falls from an upper-story window.
Paul survives a venomous snakebite on Malta without apparent harm.
Jesus foretells a period of great tribulation and warns of severe distress; Revelation also refers to people who come out of great tribulation.
Daniel speaks of a desolating act; Jesus later refers to the abomination of desolation.
John warns of antichrists who deny the truth about Jesus Christ.
Paul describes a lawless figure who exalts himself and deceives many.
Revelation describes a mark associated with allegiance to the beast and restrictions on trade.
Revelation identifies 666 as the number of the beast.
The first four seals reveal riders commonly understood to represent conquest, war, famine, and death.
The Lamb opens a sequence of seals revealing judgments and heavenly scenes.
Seven trumpet blasts introduce a series of judgments in John's vision.
Seven angels pour out bowls representing the final plagues in Revelation.
Two prophetic witnesses testify, are killed, and are raised.
John sees a woman, a dragon, and conflict surrounding the woman's child and offspring.
John sees a beast rising from the sea and receiving authority.
A second beast deceives the earth and promotes worship of the first beast.
Revelation portrays the downfall and judgment of Babylon the great.
aliases: The Fall of Babylon the Great

entries.description: Unclean spirits gather kings for battle at a place called Armageddon.
Jesus describes the coming of the Son of Man in power and glory, when his angels gather the elect.
aliases: The Sign of the Son of Man

entries.term: Caught Up to Meet the Lord
entries.description: Paul describes deceased believers rising and living believers being caught up to meet the Lord.
Paul argues that Christ's resurrection guarantees the hope of resurrection.
Revelation 20 describes Satan being bound for a thousand years and those who reign with Christ during that period.
An angel binds Satan so he cannot deceive the nations for a thousand years.
Ezekiel prophesies an attack by Gog and his allies and God's intervention against them.
John sees the dead judged before a great white throne according to what is written in books.
Revelation describes the book of life, and those not found written in it are cast into the lake of fire.
John sees a renewed heaven and earth where God dwells with his people.
John sees the holy city, New Jerusalem, descending from heaven in glory.
Heaven rejoices at the marriage supper of the Lamb.
aliases: The Marriage Supper of the Lamb

entries.description: Joel warns of the coming day of the Lord and calls for repentance.
Daniel receives a prophecy concerning seventy weeks appointed for his people and city.
Daniel sees a little horn emerge in a vision of a fourth beast.
Paul teaches that salvation is God's gift received through faith, not earned by works.
Jesus tells Nicodemus that a person must be born again to see the kingdom of God.
The Trinity is a Christian theological term for one God as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The cited verses name all three, but do not use the word Trinity.
Original sin is a theological term for humanity’s condition in relation to Adam’s sin. Romans 5 contrasts sin and death through Adam with righteousness and life through Christ.
Paul explains how God declares people righteous through faith in Jesus Christ.
God's will for believers to be set apart for holiness and to avoid sexual immorality.
Paul describes forgiveness and deliverance through Christ's blood.
Paul explains how God deals with sin justly through Christ's redeeming work.
God brings people into a restored relationship with himself through Christ.
Believers receive the Spirit of adoption and are called children and heirs of God.
Paul describes God's choosing of believers in Christ before the foundation of the world.
Paul writes that God predestined believers in Christ according to his purpose, and speaks of those foreknown and predestined in Romans.
Peter calls his hearers to turn from sin and return to God.
Paul connects baptism with participation in Christ's death and resurrection.
Paul recounts Jesus' institution of the bread and cup in remembrance of him.
Jesus promises another Comforter, the Spirit of truth, to remain with his followers.
Paul lists different spiritual gifts given by the Spirit for the common good.
Paul lists qualities such as love, joy, peace, and patience produced by the Spirit.
Paul compares the church to one body with many members.
Peter describes believers as a holy and royal priesthood.
Humanity is created in God's image.
John identifies the Word as God and active in creation.
The eternal Word becomes flesh and dwells among people.
aliases: in the beginning was the word

entries.description: Paul explains the transformation of the body in resurrection.
Jesus promises everlasting life to those who believe in him.
Paul teaches that all must appear before Christ's judgment seat.
Jesus warns against blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.
James argues that genuine faith is demonstrated through action.
Jesus continually intercedes for those who draw near to God through him.
Paul teaches that anyone in Christ is a new creation.
Paul describes spiritual armor believers are to put on to stand against evil.
Jesus commands his followers to love their enemies and pray for persecutors.
Jesus teaches that forgiving others is connected to receiving God's forgiveness.
Paul urges believers to rejoice always, pray without ceasing, and give thanks in everything.
Jesus teaches his followers not to make a show of fasting.
Malachi rebukes Israel for withholding tithes and offerings; Jesus also rebukes religious leaders who tithe while neglecting weightier matters of the law.
Paul encourages cheerful, generous giving and trust in God's provision.
Genesis describes the creation of woman and the union of husband and wife.
Paul instructs children to obey parents and fathers to raise children without provoking them.
The commandment tells Israel to honor father and mother; Paul repeats it when instructing children in the church.
James encourages steadfastness through trials because testing develops endurance.
Paul teaches that God provides a way to endure temptation.
James warns that the tongue can cause great harm and is difficult to control.
Jesus warns against judging others while ignoring one's own faults.
Jesus calls peacemakers blessed and identifies them as God's children.
Paul calls believers to humility by pointing to Christ's self-giving example.
Paul describes learning contentment in both need and abundance through Christ's strength.
Paul urges prayer instead of anxiety and directs believers to dwell on what is good.
Paul portrays the Christian struggle as spiritual and calls believers to stand firm in God's strength.
Paul describes love's character, endurance, and enduring importance.
aliases: The Greatest of These Is Love

entries.description: Jesus tells people to treat others as they themselves want to be treated.
Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come to him for rest.
Believers are encouraged to persevere while looking to Jesus.
Paul urges believers to be transformed through the renewal of their minds.
aliases: Do Not Be Conformed to This World

entries.description: Paul instructs believers to do everything for God's glory.
Paul calls believers to serve one another through love.
Paul calls believers to restore someone overtaken in a fault gently, bear one another’s burdens, and examine their own conduct.
Paul encourages believers to share with those in need and practice hospitality.
James describes pure religion as caring for orphans and widows in distress.
Jesus tells his hearers to seek God's kingdom and righteousness above material concerns.
Jesus gives the twelve apostles authority and names them before sending them out.
A Jewish religious group criticized by Jesus for hypocrisy and misplaced priorities in Matthew 23.
A Jewish group is described as denying resurrection.
Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman amid longstanding social divisions.
Members of the tribe of Levi assigned duties related to worship and the sanctuary.
Numbers 6 describes the Nazarite vow of dedication to the LORD, including abstinence from wine and restrictions concerning hair and contact with the dead.
Mysterious figures mentioned in Genesis in connection with ancient mighty men.
Heavenly beings in Isaiah's vision who proclaim God's holiness.
Heavenly beings placed to guard the way to the tree of life after Eden.
People of the nations outside Israel, brought near to God through Christ.
Tax collectors, often called publicans in the KJV, appear in Jesus' teaching.
Experts in the written law whom Jesus warns against seeking status and exploiting others.
Jesus is brought before the high priest and the council, where witnesses testify and he is questioned about his identity.
Hebrews presents Jesus as the great high priest who has passed into the heavens and can sympathize with human weakness.
Jesus warns that false prophets can appear harmless but are known by their fruit.
A sacred chest made for the covenant testimony, with a mercy seat and cherubim.
The portable sanctuary God instructed Israel to construct for worship in the wilderness.
The temple Solomon built in Jerusalem according to detailed plans.
The rebuilt Jerusalem temple completed after the exile and dedicated by returning exiles.
The gold cover of the ark is the place associated with God's meeting with Moses.
The innermost sanctuary separated by a veil and associated with God's presence.
God commands an altar for burning incense.
God instructs Moses to make a golden lampstand with six branches extending from its central shaft, for seven lamps.
Bread is placed regularly before the Lord in the sanctuary.
The temple curtain is torn when Jesus dies.
A tree in Eden associated with life, later appearing in Revelation's new creation.
The tree in Eden whose forbidden fruit Adam and Eve ate.
A well near Sychar where Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman.
John the Baptist identifies Jesus as the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sin.
A title for Christ in John's vision, linking him with Judah and David.
Jesus describes himself as the true bread from heaven who gives life.
Jesus offers living water to a Samaritan woman as a picture of lasting life.
Paul describes Christ as the cornerstone of God's household.
Jesus promises Peter the keys of the kingdom of heaven and speaks of binding and loosing.
Paul identifies faith as a shield against the evil one's attacks.
God gives Israel commandments through Moses at Sinai.
God promises Noah that a flood will never again destroy all living creatures and gives the rainbow as a sign.
God promises Abraham descendants, land, and blessing extending to all families of the earth.
God establishes covenant obligations with Israel after the exodus from Egypt.
God promises David an enduring royal house and kingdom.
God promises a new covenant marked by forgiveness and his law written on hearts.
The commandment sets apart the seventh day as a day of rest.
Israel is commanded to eat unleavened bread for seven days.
Israel celebrates a harvest feast seven weeks after the counting begins.
aliases: The Feast of Weeks at Sinai

entries.description: A day of rest and trumpet memorial is commanded in the seventh month.
The annual day when the high priest makes atonement for Israel's sins.
Israel is commanded to dwell in booths during a seven-day feast.
The fiftieth year is proclaimed as a jubilee, with liberty and the return of people to their families and ancestral property.
The law commands release of certain debts every seven years.
God designates cities of refuge where someone who kills another unintentionally can flee and receive a hearing.
A close relative may redeem family land that has been sold.
Circumcision is given to Abraham as a sign of God's covenant with his household.
Israel is instructed to bring the first sheaf of the harvest to the priest, who waves it before the Lord.
The Jews establish an annual feast recalling their deliverance.
The Holy Spirit comes upon believers at Pentecost and Peter preaches to the crowd.
Matthias is chosen to take Judas's place among the apostles.
Ananias and Sapphira die after lying about the proceeds of a property sale.
Seven men are appointed to address a dispute over daily distribution.
Stephen is stoned after testifying before the council.
Philip explains Isaiah to an Ethiopian traveler and baptizes him.
aliases: The Conversion of the Ethiopian Eunuch

entries.description: Saul encounters the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus and is baptized.
Peter visits Cornelius, and the Holy Spirit comes upon Gentile hearers.
The apostles and elders in Jerusalem consider whether Gentile believers must be circumcised and keep the law of Moses.
Paul and Silas pray and sing while imprisoned in Philippi. After an earthquake opens the prison doors, the jailer and his household hear the gospel.
aliases: Paul and Silas Sing in Prison

entries.description: Paul speaks in Athens about the God unknown to his listeners and the resurrection.
During a voyage toward Rome, Paul and the others survive a storm and shipwreck; afterward they reach Malta.
The Bereans examine the Scriptures daily to evaluate Paul's teaching.
Priscilla and Aquila explain God's way more accurately to Apollos.
Paul addresses the elders from Ephesus and urges them to shepherd the church faithfully.
Enoch is described as walking with God before God took him.
Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blesses Abram.

entries.term: Hagar and Ishmael in the Wilderness
entries.description: God hears Ishmael and provides water for Hagar and her son.
Jacob receives the blessing Isaac intended for Esau.
Joseph's special coat and dreams intensify his brothers' resentment.
Joseph discloses his identity to his brothers in Egypt.
Moses is rescued from the Nile and raised in Pharaoh's household.
God provides drinkable water for Israel at Marah.

entries.term: Giving of the Law at Sinai
entries.description: Israel encounters God at Sinai and receives the commandments.
Aaron's sons die after offering unauthorized fire before the Lord.
Korah and others challenge Moses and Aaron and face judgment.
Moses strikes a rock when instructed to speak to it.
Rahab shelters Israelite spies in Jericho.
Israel suffers defeat after Achan takes devoted items from Jericho.
Joshua calls for the sun to stand still and the moon to stop while Israel fights its enemies.
Jephthah vows to offer to the Lord whatever comes out of his house to meet him if he returns victorious; his daughter is the first to greet him.
Samson brings down the Philistine temple at his death.
The Philistines capture the ark after defeating Israel.

entries.term: Saul Consults the Medium of Endor
entries.description: Saul seeks forbidden counsel before his final battle.
aliases: Saul Consults the Medium at Endor

entries.description: Uzzah dies after reaching out to steady the ark.
The queen tests Solomon's wisdom and sees his kingdom's splendor.
Israel splits into northern and southern kingdoms under Rehoboam and Jeroboam.

entries.term: Elijah and the Widow of Zarephath
entries.description: God provides food and restores the widow's son through Elijah.
A widow's oil multiplies so she can pay her debts.
Elisha restores the Shunammite woman's son to life.
Hezekiah prays during the Assyrian threat to Jerusalem.

entries.term: Josiah Discovers the Book of the Law
entries.description: The rediscovered law prompts covenant renewal under Josiah.
Ezra reads and explains God's law to the returned community.
aliases: joy of the lord is your strength

entries.description: Daniel confesses Israel's sins and prays for Jerusalem.
Hosea's marriage to Gomer illustrates Israel's unfaithfulness; a later passage describes Hosea's renewed act of love without naming the woman.

entries.term: John the Baptist Prepares the Way
entries.description: John calls people to repentance and points to the coming Messiah.
aliases: prepare the way of the lord

entries.description: Jesus reads from Isaiah and speaks of the scripture's fulfillment.
Jesus teaches Nicodemus about being born again.
Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman about living water and true worship.
Jesus commissions the twelve apostles for ministry.
Jesus sends out a larger group of disciples to prepare towns for his visit.
Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God.
aliases: Peter Confesses Jesus as the Christ

entries.description: Jesus teaches that he must suffer, die, and rise again.
Jesus answers a question about paying taxes to Caesar.
aliases: is it lawful to pay taxes

entries.description: Jesus responds to accusers who bring a woman accused of adultery.
aliases: let him who is without sin

entries.description: Jesus is deeply moved and weeps before raising Lazarus from the dead.
Seven sayings of Jesus during the crucifixion, gathered from the four Gospels rather than recorded together in one passage.
aliases: my god my god why have you forsaken me
into your hands i commit my spirit

entries.term: Jesus Appears by the Sea of Tiberias
entries.description: The risen Jesus appears to disciples at the Sea of Tiberias and directs them to a large catch of fish.
aliases: The Second Miraculous Catch of Fish

entries.description: John records Jesus using several 'I am' descriptions of his identity and work.
aliases: i am the bread of life
i am the light of the world

entries.description: Jesus prepares his disciples for his departure and the Spirit's coming.
aliases: let not your heart be troubled
in my father's house are many mansions

entries.description: Jesus prays for himself, his disciples, and future believers.
Two debtors are forgiven unequal debts, illustrating grateful love.
A lamp is meant to give light rather than be hidden.
aliases: Parable of the Lamp on a Stand

entries.description: Servants are urged to stay ready for their master's return.

entries.term: Parable of the Faithful and Unfaithful Servant
entries.description: Jesus contrasts faithful stewardship with abusive neglect.
Jesus teaches humility in fulfilling one's duty.
aliases: we have only done our duty

entries.description: Jesus compares obedience to building a house on a firm foundation.
The fig tree's leaves illustrate recognizing signs of a season.
aliases: The Fig Tree as a Sign

entries.description: Servants are entrusted with money while a nobleman is away.
Jesus illustrates counting the cost before beginning a project.

entries.term: Parable of the King Going to War
entries.description: A king assesses his strength before entering a battle.
Jesus heals Simon's mother-in-law of a fever.
Jesus delivers a Gentile woman's daughter from an unclean spirit.

entries.term: Healing the Blind Men near Jericho
entries.description: Jesus restores sight to two blind men near Jericho.
aliases: Jesus heals two blind men at Jericho

entries.description: Jesus heals a man on the Sabbath at a Pharisee's house.
aliases: Jesus Heals a Man with Dropsy

entries.description: Peter tells Aeneas to rise after years of paralysis.

entries.term: Paul Heals a Lame Man at Lystra
entries.description: A man unable to walk from birth is healed through Paul's ministry.

entries.term: Paul Casts Out a Spirit of Divination
entries.description: Paul commands a spirit to leave a slave girl in Philippi.
God works unusual healings through Paul's ministry.
Micah foretells a ruler in Israel coming from Bethlehem Ephratah, a prophecy connected with Jesus in Matthew.
Isaiah describes a servant who suffers on behalf of others.
aliases: by his stripes we are healed

entries.description: Isaiah speaks of a child called Immanuel, a passage Matthew applies to Jesus.
A ruler from Jesse's line is described as righteous and Spirit-filled.
Jeremiah foretells seventy years of Babylonian rule and promises that God will bring his people back after that period.
Joel foretells an outpouring of God's Spirit, cited by Peter at Pentecost.
Daniel sees four beasts and a vision of divine judgment and kingship.

entries.term: Son of Man Coming with Clouds

Jesus prays for those who have received his word.

entries.term: The Valley of Dry Bones Explained
entries.description: God identifies the dry bones as the whole house of Israel and promises to bring them into their land and put his Spirit in them.
The psalm urges delight, trust, and patient rest in the Lord.
Believers are encouraged to cast their anxieties on God.
Believers are urged to persevere while looking to Jesus.
Aaron’s rod buds as a sign confirming his priestly calling.
The apostles testify despite arrest and orders to stop preaching.
The disciples are first called Christians in Antioch.
Faith is defined as the assurance of things hoped for, illustrated by the faithful lives of Abel, Noah, Abraham, Moses, and others.
aliases: faith is the substance of things hoped for
without faith it is impossible to please god

entries.term: For God So Loved the World
entries.description: God gives his only Son so that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.

entries.term: All Things Work Together for Good
entries.description: God works all things together for the good of those who love him and are called according to his purpose.
God tells the exiles in Babylon that he has plans for their welfare, a future, and a hope.
aliases: for i know the plans i have for you

entries.description: Jesus teaches his followers not to retaliate against evil, but to turn the other cheek and go the extra mile.
After the final plague Pharaoh lets Israel go, and the people leave Egypt after 430 years.
Widowed Ruth refuses to leave her mother-in-law Naomi and returns with her to Bethlehem.
aliases: where you go i will go
your people will be my people

entries.description: Jacob serves Laban seven years for Rachel, is given Leah instead, and serves seven more years for Rachel.
Methuselah, the son of Enoch and grandfather of Noah, lives 969 years.
Isaiah's taunt against the king of Babylon describes the shining one cast down from heaven, a passage traditionally associated with the fall of Satan.
Angels are ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation.
aliases: he will give his angels charge over you

entries.description: Michael, the great prince who protects God's people, disputes with the devil and fights the dragon in heaven.
God declares himself the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.
aliases: i am the alpha and omega

entries.description: Christ commends the church at Ephesus for its labor and discernment but rebukes it for abandoning its first love.
Christ encourages the suffering church at Smyrna to be faithful unto death and receive the crown of life.
Christ commends the church at Pergamum, which lives where Satan's throne is, but warns it against false teaching.
Christ praises the growing works of the church at Thyatira but rebukes it for tolerating the teaching of Jezebel.
Christ warns the church at Sardis that it has a name for being alive but is dead, and calls it to wake up.
aliases: you have a name that you are alive

entries.description: Christ sets an open door before the faithful church at Philadelphia and promises to keep it from the hour of trial.
Christ rebukes the lukewarm church at Laodicea and stands at the door and knocks.
aliases: i stand at the door and knock

entries.description: John is in the Spirit on the Lord's day, and the early believers gather on the first day of the week.
aliases: in the spirit on the lord's day

entries.description: Paul gives instructions about head coverings and order when men and women pray or prophesy in worship.
John distinguishes between sin that leads to death and sin that does not, and encourages prayer for a sinning brother.

entries.term: For Such a Time as This
entries.description: Mordecai urges Esther to plead with the king for her people, and she resolves to go to him though it may cost her life.
Angels announce Jesus' birth to shepherds in the fields near Bethlehem, and the shepherds go to see the child in the manger.
aliases: glory to god in the highest

entries.description: Herod, furious that the wise men did not return, orders the killing of the young boys in Bethlehem.
aliases: killing of the infants in Bethlehem

entries.description: God brings the animals to Adam to name, and none is found as a suitable helper for him.
God forms the first woman from Adam's rib and brings her to him.
Sarah bears Isaac in her old age, as God had promised Abraham.
The elders of Israel ask Samuel for a king like the other nations, and God tells Samuel to grant it.
Samuel privately anoints Saul as Israel's first king, and later presents him to the people.

entries.term: David Plays the Harp for Saul
entries.description: David's music soothes King Saul when a distressing spirit troubles him.
The Philistines place the captured ark in Dagon's temple, suffer plagues, and send it back to Israel.
Isaiah sees the Lord in the temple, is cleansed with a burning coal, and answers, 'Here am I; send me.'
Gabriel tells the priest Zechariah that his wife Elizabeth will bear John, and Zechariah is made unable to speak.
Mary visits her relative Elizabeth, and the child in Elizabeth's womb leaps; Mary sings the Magnificat.
Elizabeth gives birth to John, Zechariah confirms his name and speaks again, and prophesies.
Philip brings Nathanael to Jesus, who says he saw him under the fig tree.
aliases: can anything good come out of Nazareth

entries.description: Jesus teaches on level ground with blessings and woes, love for enemies, and the call to be merciful.
aliases: blessed are you who are poor

entries.term: Jesus Anointed by a Sinful Woman
entries.description: A sinful woman weeps on Jesus' feet, wipes them with her hair, and anoints them at a Pharisee's house.
aliases: woman washes Jesus' feet with tears

entries.description: Judas returns the silver, then hangs himself; the priests use the money to buy the Potter's Field.
Jesus is questioned by Caiaphas and the council, declares he is the Christ, and is condemned for blasphemy.
The crowd chooses Barabbas over Jesus, and Pilate washes his hands before handing Jesus over.
Roman soldiers dress Jesus in a purple robe, press a crown of thorns on his head, and mock him as king.

entries.term: Simon of Cyrene Carries the Cross
entries.description: Soldiers compel Simon of Cyrene to carry Jesus' cross on the way to Golgotha.

entries.term: Soldiers Cast Lots for Jesus' Garments
entries.description: The soldiers divide Jesus' clothes and cast lots for his seamless tunic.
Darkness covers the land from noon until three, and Jesus cries out and gives up his spirit.
The centurion at the cross sees how Jesus died and declares he was truly the Son of God.
aliases: truly this was the Son of God

entries.description: Pilate lets the priests seal and guard Jesus' tomb; after the resurrection the guards are bribed to spread a false story.
The risen Jesus appears among the disciples behind locked doors, shows his wounds, eats, and gives them the Spirit.
aliases: Jesus appears in the upper room

entries.description: Paul asks three times for his thorn to be removed, and the Lord answers, 'My grace is sufficient for you.'
aliases: when I am weak I am strong

entries.description: Paul urges Philemon to receive his runaway slave Onesimus back as a brother.
On the island of Patmos, John sees the glorified Christ among seven lampstands and is told to write what he sees.

entries.term: Ezekiel's Vision of the Living Creatures
entries.description: By the river Chebar, Ezekiel sees four living creatures, wheels within wheels, and the glory of the Lord on a throne.
aliases: wheel in the middle of a wheel
